# Production Plan

This document describes how to build the YAML manager as a product-ready system while respecting the VM deployment constraints.

The companion feature/spec document is `managerplan.qmd`. That file defines what the manager should infer and validate. This file defines how to structure and build it.

## Product Context

Most authoring will happen locally on a Mac, where development can be faster and the UI can be polished.

The same backend must also work inside the isolated company VM. The VM can receive copied code, but it cannot pull from git, and code cannot be copied back out. Updates therefore need to be easy to transfer manually.

The long-term product should support two presentation layers:

- A polished, responsive local interface for demos and richer authoring.
- A spartan VM-compatible interface that works within the DSVM package limits.

Both interfaces should use the same backend manager logic.

## Deployment Constraints

The VM constraints shape the architecture:

- Keep the number of files small.
- Avoid exotic dependencies.
- Prefer packages already listed in `VM Data/DSVM Plugins.yaml`.
- Make the backend copy-paste deployable.
- Do not require git access from the VM.
- Do not require internet access from the VM.
- Do not require the VM UI to be as polished as the local Mac UI.
- Keep the existing server-side/local-side SQL generation pipeline intact until the new manager is trusted.

## File Strategy

The portable VM version should use as few files as practical:

```text
scripts/makeYaml.py
YAMLs/template.yaml
YAMLs/recipes.yaml
```

Optional later files:

```text
YAMLs/<Project_Name>_Full.yaml
manager_report.md
vm_gui.py
local_gui.py
```

The backend should start as one well-organized Python file, `scripts/makeYaml.py`, rather than a package spread across many modules.

The script should be movable. It should resolve default paths relative to its own location:

```text
scripts/makeYaml.py
../YAMLs/template.yaml
../YAMLs/recipes.yaml
```

All paths should also be configurable with CLI flags.

This is not because one large file is aesthetically ideal. It is because the VM copy-update workflow rewards fewer moving parts.

## Backend And GUI Split

The backend should be interface-agnostic.

Dependency direction:

```text
CLI -> makeYaml.py
GUI -> makeYaml.py
VM SQL scripts -> finished YAML
```

The backend should not import or know about the GUI.

The GUI should read structured outputs from the backend:

- inferred variables
- table input requirements
- output columns
- upload validation
- errors
- warnings
- expanded cohort/group names
- graph/node metadata

This lets a rich Mac UI and a spartan VM UI display the same information differently.

## Existing Pipeline Placement

Current conceptual flow:

```text
human-authored YAML
-> makeSql-style scripts
-> server-side SQL
-> server instance variable
-> local-side SQL
-> execution manager
```

New flow:

```text
YAMLs/template.yaml + YAMLs/recipes.yaml
-> scripts/makeYaml.py
-> finished definitive YAML
-> existing makeSql-style scripts
-> server-side SQL
-> server instance variable
-> local-side SQL
-> execution manager
```

The first goal is to make `makeYaml.py` produce the same kind of finished YAML that the existing SQL scripts already understand.

## Python Dependency Choices

Prefer DSVM-available packages:

- `ruamel.yaml` for loading/writing YAML while preserving comments and readable formatting.
- `pyyaml` as a fallback if `ruamel.yaml` is unavailable.
- `jinja2` for rendering manager-side expressions like `sql_condition(...)`.

The backend should hide the specific YAML library behind helper functions:

```python
load_yaml(path)
dump_yaml(data, path)
```

This keeps the rest of the manager insulated if the implementation needs to fall back from `ruamel.yaml` to `pyyaml`.

Avoid making the core manager depend on GUI frameworks.

Potential GUI packages listed in the DSVM plugin file:

- `streamlit`
- `dash`
- `dash-cytoscape`

These should remain optional interface layers, not backend requirements.

## `makeYaml.py` Internal Structure

The file can stay physically single-file while remaining logically modular.

Suggested sections:

```python
# =============================================================================
# Imports and constants
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Data structures
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# YAML loading and writing
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Recipe import
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Normalization
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Inference
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Validation
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Rendering
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Expansion: multipliers and batching
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Public API
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# CLI
# =============================================================================
```

The internal organization should make it easy to split into modules later if deployment constraints change.

## Backend Public API

The backend should expose functions that the CLI and GUI can both call.

Suggested minimum API:

```python
def compile_yaml(template_path, recipes_path, output_path=None):
    ...

def validate_yaml(template_path, recipes_path):
    ...

def inspect_recipes(recipes_path):
    ...
```

`compile_yaml` should return a structured result object/dictionary, not only print messages.

Example result shape:

```python
{
    "ok": True,
    "errors": [],
    "warnings": [],
    "finished_yaml": {...},
    "analysis": {
        "cohorts": [...],
        "uploads": [...],
        "required_vars": {...},
        "required_table_columns": {...},
        "output_columns": {...},
    },
    "graph": {
        "nodes": [...],
        "edges": [...],
    },
}
```

The CLI can print this. The GUI can visualize it.

## CLI Goals

The first production interface should be CLI-only.

Initial command:

```bash
python scripts/makeYaml.py --template YAMLs/template.yaml --recipes YAMLs/recipes.yaml
```

Useful future commands:

```bash
python scripts/makeYaml.py --validate --template YAMLs/template.yaml
python scripts/makeYaml.py --template YAMLs/MyProject.yaml --out YAMLs/MyProject_Full.yaml
python scripts/makeYaml.py --inspect-recipes
python scripts/makeYaml.py --report --template YAMLs/template.yaml --report-out manager_report.md
```

The CLI should:

- Print errors clearly.
- Print warnings clearly.
- Exit nonzero on errors.
- Write the finished YAML only when validation passes, unless explicitly forced.
- Provide a built-in TDD/self-test mode that travels with `makeYaml.py`.
- Never overwrite the pre-YAML template in place.
- Default output names from `project_folder` plus a configurable suffix.

Default output naming:

```text
project_folder: "Test Run"
OUTPUT_SUFFIX = "_Full"
-> YAMLs/Test_Run_Full.yaml
```

The CLI should allow overriding output location and suffix:

```bash
python scripts/makeYaml.py --template YAMLs/template.yaml --suffix _Full
python scripts/makeYaml.py --template YAMLs/template.yaml --out YAMLs/custom_output.yaml
```

TDD command:

```bash
python scripts/makeYaml.py --tdd
```

Optional focused TDD commands:

```bash
python scripts/makeYaml.py --tdd loading
python scripts/makeYaml.py --tdd inference
python scripts/makeYaml.py --tdd rendering
python scripts/makeYaml.py --tdd multipliers
python scripts/makeYaml.py --tdd batching
```

## GUI Goals

The local Mac GUI can be polished and responsive.

The VM GUI should be modest but functional.

Both should use the backend API rather than reimplementing manager logic.

GUI capabilities should eventually include:

- Recipe browser.
- Batching recipe browser.
- Upload table validator.
- Required variable display.
- Required input column display.
- Node/edge view of table dependencies.
- Warnings and errors.
- Preview of expanded cohort names.
- Preview of final YAML.

The GUI should be a viewer/editor around the backend, not a separate source of truth.

## Development Phases

### Phase 1: Core Compiler Skeleton

Goal: load YAML, import recipes, write a finished YAML without multipliers/batching.

Features:

- Load `YAMLs/template.yaml` by default, with CLI override support.
- Load `YAMLs/recipes.yaml` by default, with CLI override support.
- Read `batching_recipes` without using them yet.
- Import recipe cohorts.
- Overlay cohort-specific fields.
- Normalize `dest_table`.
- Normalize top-level `vars`.
- Write a finished YAML.
- Return structured result with errors/warnings.

TDD checks:

- Pass: load valid template YAML.
- Pass: load valid recipes YAML.
- Fail: malformed YAML reports a useful error.
- Pass: import a recipe into a concrete cohort.
- Pass: cohort-specific fields override recipe defaults.
- Pass: `dest_table` defaults to cohort `name`.

### Phase 2: Inference And Validation

Goal: make the manager useful as a safety checker.

Features:

- Infer `{{variables}}`.
- Infer variable-backed table inputs from `##JVM_{{TableVar}} AS alias`.
- Infer required input columns from alias usage.
- Discover output columns from `columns`.
- Infer `PKTable` from the single `type: PK` cohort.
- Validate missing variables.
- Validate missing required table columns.
- Validate upload references.
- Validate CSV upload headers where possible.
- Emit warnings for unused vars and compatibility fields.

TDD checks:

- Pass: infer `{{min_date_key}}`, `{{max_date_key}}`, and `{{PKTable}}`.
- Pass: infer `PKTable` from a single `type: PK` cohort.
- Pass: explicit `vars.PKTable` overrides auto-detected `PKTable`.
- Fail: missing required variable is reported.
- Fail: multiple PK cohorts prevent `PKTable` inference.
- Fail: no PK cohort prevents `PKTable` inference when required.
- Pass: infer input table columns from `##JVM_{{PKTable}} AS pk` and `pk.ColumnName`.
- Fail: input table missing a required column.
- Pass: referenced CSV upload exists and has required columns.
- Fail: referenced upload file is missing.
- Fail: referenced CSV upload lacks a required column.

### Phase 3: Manager-Side Rendering

Goal: support user-friendly expressions before VM handoff.

Features:

- Implement `sql_condition(column, value_var)`.
- Infer `IN` versus `LIKE`.
- Support scalar and list values.
- Warn on `_` in `LIKE` values.
- Render final YAML with plain SQL-like strings only.
- Ensure the VM never needs to understand manager helper expressions.

TDD checks:

- Pass: scalar value renders as `=`.
- Pass: list without wildcards renders as `IN`.
- Pass: single wildcard value renders as `LIKE`.
- Pass: multiple wildcard values render as `LIKE ... OR LIKE ...`.
- Warn: `_` appears in a value rendered with `LIKE`.
- Fail: `sql_condition` references a missing variable.
- Pass: final YAML contains rendered SQL text, not `sql_condition(...)`.

### Phase 4: Multipliers

Goal: expand cohort groups safely.

Features:

- Support `stage: during_build`.
- Support `stage: split_after_build`.
- Support `applies_to: PKTable`.
- Support `column`/`values` split syntax.
- Support advanced `where` syntax for complex splits.
- Combine multiplier levels as Cartesian products.
- Resolve group-specific `PKTable`.
- Validate split columns against the target table output schema.
- Preserve control metadata such as `role: control` and `row_mult`.

TDD checks:

- Pass: `during_build` multiplier applies level vars before rendering.
- Pass: `split_after_build` multiplier uses `applies_to`, `column`, and `values`.
- Pass: split values use the same `IN` versus `LIKE` inference as `sql_condition`.
- Fail: `split_after_build` references a missing target column.
- Pass: multiplier levels combine as a Cartesian product.
- Pass: each expanded group gets its own resolved `PKTable`.
- Pass: control metadata is preserved in the expanded output.

### Phase 5: Batching

Goal: split expanded groups by PK batches.

Features:

- Read `batching_recipes`.
- Support preset shorthand such as `state`, `sex`, and `chunk`.
- Support `chunk: 2000`.
- Support multiple batching rules in order.
- Split PK rows only.
- Make downstream fact cohorts join to the matching batch-specific PK table.
- Validate batching columns against PK output schema.
- Generate predictable batch suffixes.

TDD checks:

- Pass: load `batching_recipes`.
- Pass: `state` preset resolves to `StateOrProvinceAbbreviation`.
- Pass: `sex` preset resolves to `Sex`.
- Pass: `chunk: 2000` resolves to row chunk batching.
- Pass: numeric shorthand `- 2000` resolves to row chunk batching.
- Pass: multiple batching rules compose in order.
- Fail: batching preset requires a PK column that is missing.
- Pass: downstream fact cohorts use the batch-specific PK table.

### Phase 6: Cosmos/Dual Expansion

Goal: model COSMOS, SneakPeek, and Dual behavior.

Features:

- Normalize `cosmos_db`.
- Support `COSMOS`.
- Support `COSMOS_SneakPeek`.
- Support `Dual`/`both`.
- Treat `Dual`/`both` like an additional expansion dimension.
- Generate `_sp` or other agreed suffixes consistently.
- Ensure SneakPeek and non-SneakPeek runs do not collide in table names.

TDD checks:

- Pass: `COSMOS` produces only standard Cosmos groups.
- Pass: `COSMOS_SneakPeek` produces only SneakPeek groups.
- Pass: `Dual`/`both` produces standard and SneakPeek groups.
- Pass: SneakPeek groups get the agreed suffix.
- Fail: unsupported `cosmos_db` value reports a useful error.

### Phase 7: Reports And Debuggability

Goal: make the manager easy to trust.

Features:

- Markdown validation report.
- Expanded cohort list.
- Upload validation table.
- Variable source table showing global/local/generated values.
- Required column compatibility table.
- Warning summary.
- Final YAML preview location.

TDD checks:

- Pass: report includes errors.
- Pass: report includes warnings.
- Pass: report includes upload validation summary.
- Pass: report includes required column compatibility summary.
- Pass: report includes expanded cohort names.

### Phase 8: Interfaces

Goal: build UI layers after the backend is stable.

Mac/local interface:

- Rich authoring experience.
- Responsive visual graph.
- Recipe and batching recipe explorer.
- More polished validation display.

VM-compatible interface:

- Minimal dependencies.
- Uses the same backend API.
- May be CLI-first, Streamlit, or Dash depending on what works best in the VM.

## Testing Strategy

Keep tests close to the manager and make them available in the VM without extra files or frameworks.

The first testing system should be an embedded TDD harness inside `makeYaml.py`.

Required command:

```bash
python scripts/makeYaml.py --tdd
```

The TDD run should:

- Use small embedded YAML examples.
- Avoid any database connection.
- Avoid internet access.
- Avoid requiring a separate `tests/` directory.
- Print `PASS`, `FAIL`, and `WARN` lines.
- Show expected versus actual output for failures.
- Exit nonzero if any test fails.

Example output:

```text
TDD Results

PASS  loading.valid_template
PASS  recipes.import_recipe
PASS  inference.required_vars
PASS  validation.missing_var_error
PASS  rendering.sql_condition_in
PASS  rendering.sql_condition_like
WARN  rendering.like_underscore_warning
FAIL  multipliers.split_missing_column

Summary: 7 passed, 1 warned as expected, 1 failed
```

Each new feature should include:

- One happy-path test.
- One failure-path test.
- One warning-path test when warnings are part of the feature.

Recommended test groups:

- `loading`
- `recipes`
- `inference`
- `validation`
- `uploads`
- `rendering`
- `multipliers`
- `batching`
- `cosmos`
- `reports`

The embedded tests should exercise the public API where possible, especially `compile_yaml(...)` and `validate_yaml(...)`, instead of reaching deeply into private helper functions.

This keeps the tests aligned with real user behavior and future GUI behavior.

Potential later approach:

- Add `tests/` locally on the Mac.
- Add `pytest` tests for faster local iteration.
- Keep VM deployment focused on `scripts/makeYaml.py`, `YAMLs/template.yaml`, and `YAMLs/recipes.yaml`.

The local `tests/` folder should be optional. The VM-safe `--tdd` harness remains the portable baseline.

## Copy-Update Workflow

Because the VM cannot pull from git, updates should be easy to transfer.

Preferred VM update set:

```text
scripts/makeYaml.py
YAMLs/recipes.yaml
YAMLs/template.yaml
```

Optional:

```text
vm_gui.py
```

Avoid spreading backend logic across many small helper files unless deployment constraints change.

## Non-Goals For The First Version

The first manager should not:

- Replace existing SQL generation scripts.
- Require a GUI.
- Require internet access.
- Require database connections for validation.
- Parse arbitrary SQL perfectly.
- Preserve all comments/formatting in generated YAML.
- Support every multiplier/batching edge case.

It should first make the common path safe, understandable, and repeatable.

## Success Criteria

The first useful version is successful when it can:

- Read `YAMLs/template.yaml` and `YAMLs/recipes.yaml`.
- Import recipes.
- Infer variables and table requirements.
- Validate uploads and required columns.
- Infer `PKTable`.
- Render `sql_condition`.
- Produce finished YAML for the existing VM SQL pipeline.
- Return structured data that a future GUI can visualize.

The production-ready version is successful when:

- The same backend supports CLI, Mac GUI, and VM UI.
- Most user mistakes are caught before VM execution.
- Multipliers and batching remove repetitive manual YAML authoring.
- The VM deployment remains small enough to update by direct copy-paste.
